messages:
Zoe M: Quick routing/help — we're converting a contractor (Samir P) to a 0.7 FTE perm IC3. Proposed FTE comp $130,000 -> prorated $91,000. At 70% the S3 prorated cap is $88,000, so we're ~3k over. Also benefits eligibility kicks in at 75% FTE per policy, candidate expects medical — can we get an exception or guidance? Preferred start 2026-03-15, fallback 2026-04-01.

Priya - People Ops: Thanks Zoe. Routing checklist: manager justification + org head signoff; finance confirm prorate & funding; comp committee for >$2k variance; benefits for eligibility exception/request; legal for contractor->employee conversion and any local tax implications for remote states. Paste justification and org code and I'll open ticket.

Zoe M: Manager justification: "Samir has led reliability work on the routing layer for 9 months as contractor. Conversion reduces ramp time and saves ~$30k over 6 months vs extending contract. Critical for Q2 roadmap and will mentor two junior hires." Org code ENG-RT-03. Candidate prefers base increase over equity; will accept one-time cash only as last resort.

Carlos F: Finance sees prorate math ok. Need chargeback center and confirm budget this FY. On benefits: if candidate is <75% FTE we usually don't grant full medical; exceptions are rare and need VP People sign-off plus budget note for benefits cost. Also confirm payroll cutoff for Mar start.

Anya (Comp Chair): We'll add to comp committee agenda. At ~3k prorate variance committee typically either approves a small base exception or recommends a one-time cash top-up. If candidate prefers base and refuses equity, comp will escalate to VP People for approval if committee supports the uplift. Please attach benchmarking.

Payroll Bot: FYI payroll cutoff for 2026-03-15 active start is 2026-03-01. If approvals miss cutoff earliest active payroll will be 2026-04-15. Also confirm last contractor invoice date to avoid overlap.

Zoe M: Last contractor invoice planned 2026-03-10. Chargeback ENG-RT-03-01. Candidate accepts 0.7 FTE but wants medical; told them 75% is required but asked if an exception possible.

Priya - People Ops: I'll open HR ticket HR-2798456123 and route to finance@, comp-committee@, benefits@, legal@. Please reply with `+approve` or `-need info`. Will track VP escalation if comp recommends exception and benefits requests exemption.

Sam-bot: Ticket HR-2798456123 created by Zoe M. Link: https://redwood.internal/hr/HR-2798456123

Legal Ops: Quick flag: contractor->employee conversion needs final written offer, IP assignment, and confirmation of last contractor invoice to avoid overlap. If candidate is remote in a different state, we need to confirm state tax withholding and local benefits compliance.

Carlos F: Budget holds for 0.7 FTE in ENG-RT this FY. If comp committee approves base uplift, we'll calculate annualized impact; VP sign-off required for annualized uplift >$4k. At prorated level this equates to ~3k so likely comp committee + VP review path.

Anya (Comp Chair): +approve to put on committee agenda (not final). Please attach benchmarks and manager note. If committee supports uplift, we'll document exception and escalate to VP People for benefits exception and final sign-off.

Priya - People Ops: Thanks all  I'll update HR-2798456123 with attachments and ping VP People if comp favors base uplift. Zoe please ask candidate to confirm willingness to accept benefits pro-rata if exception denied.

Zoe M: Will confirm with candidate by EOD. Thanks :thumbsup:
